editorial.headline: Plastic Wrapping Retail: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Plastic wrapping retail is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet Bali currently blocks PMA registration under its permanent risk-based moratorium.
editorial.body:
An overseas investor cannot register this activity through PMA in Bali today. KBLI 47796 covers the retail trade in plastic wrapping goods: plastic sold by weight, rubbish bags and plastic bags. It is a tightly defined retail activity focused on these everyday packaging items. The scope identifies the goods in question clearly, including plastic sold by weight, rubbish bags and plastic bags, and notes that it extends beyond direct sales.

Nationally, however, the position is open. The record classifies the activity as open to PMA and gives a maximum foreign ownership of 100%, meaning the national framework allows full foreign ownership. Registration is open across the stated business scales—Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. For founders, that establishes the national baseline: this is a retail activity whose stated ownership ceiling is not below full foreign ownership, and whose listed scales run from Mikro through Besar.

Bali provides the decisive local qualification. The Bali record marks the activity as blocked for PMA registration because, at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Low or Medium-Low across every stated scope. Bali's island-wide, permanent moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities from PMA registration. The record connects this particular block to the Bali moratorium of May 13, 2026. For this activity, national openness does not translate into a PMA registration route in Bali.

This is therefore not a case for treating the national 100% ceiling as a proxy for present-day availability in Bali. The national classification remains relevant to the activity's general PMA position and stated scales, while the Bali restriction governs the island-wide PMA-registration reality described in the record. A founder considering plastic wrapping retail needs to hold both facts at once: the activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but Bali presently blocks its PMA registration on the risk-class ground stated here.
